title: Oriented product of topoi: site construction and universal property
statement:
Let $\mathcal C_1,\mathcal C_2,\mathcal D$ be small sites [def-weil-size-convention] whose underlying categories have finite limits and whose topologies are given by pretopologies, and let $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_1)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$, $g:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_2)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ be morphisms of topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] whose inverse images $f^{-1},g^{-1}$ extend continuous functors $\mathcal D\to\mathcal C_1$, $\mathcal D\to\mathcal C_2$ preserving finite limits. For morphisms of topoi $u,w:\mathcal E\to\mathcal F$, a $2$-morphism $u\Rightarrow w$ means a natural transformation $u_*\to w_*$ of direct-image functors (equivalently, by adjunction, $w^{-1}\to u^{-1}$).

Let $\mathcal C$ be the category whose objects are triples $(U\to V\leftarrow W)$ with $V\in\mathcal D$, $U\in\mathcal C_1$, $W\in\mathcal C_2$ and morphisms $U\to f^{-1}V$ in $\mathcal C_1$ and $W\to g^{-1}V$ in $\mathcal C_2$, with the evident morphisms. Give $\mathcal C$ the topology generated by the families $(U_i\to V_i\leftarrow W_i)\to(U\to V\leftarrow W)$ of the following three types: (a) $V_i=V$, $W_i=W$ and $(U_i\to U)$ is a covering; (b) $U_i=U$, $V_i=V$ and $(W_i\to W)$ is a covering; (c) a single map $(U\to V'\leftarrow W\times_{g^{-1}V}g^{-1}V')\to(U\to V\leftarrow W)$ induced by a morphism $V'\to V$ of $\mathcal D$ through which $U\to f^{-1}V$ factors. Put $P=\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$, the left oriented product $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_1)\overleftarrow\times_{\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)}\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_2)$. There are morphisms of topoi $p_1:P\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_1)$, $p_2:P\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_2)$ with $p_1^{-1}U=(U\to e\leftarrow e)^a$ and $p_2^{-1}W=(e\to e\leftarrow W)^a$ ($e$ the final objects, $(-)^a$ the associated sheaf), and a $2$-morphism $\tau:gp_2\Rightarrow fp_1$, such that the following holds. For every topos $\mathcal E$ with morphisms $a:\mathcal E\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_1)$, $b:\mathcal E\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_2)$ and a $2$-morphism $t:gb\Rightarrow fa$, there is a triple $(h:\mathcal E\to P,\ \alpha:p_1h\xrightarrow{\sim}a,\ \beta:p_2h\xrightarrow{\sim}b)$, unique up to unique isomorphism, such that the composite $gb\xrightarrow{g\beta^{-1}}gp_2h\xrightarrow{\tau h}fp_1h\xrightarrow{f\alpha}fa$ equals $t$. Explicitly $h^{-1}(U\to V\leftarrow W)^a=a^{-1}U\times_{(gb)^{-1}V}b^{-1}W$, where $a^{-1}U\to(gb)^{-1}V$ is $a^{-1}U\to(fa)^{-1}V$ followed by the map $(fa)^{-1}V\to(gb)^{-1}V$ given by $t$. Consequently the quadruple $(P,p_1,p_2,\tau)$ is independent of the chosen sites of definition up to unique isomorphism.

source.place: Expose XI (Illusie, Produits orientes), 1.1 (site of triples, coverings (a)-(c)), 1.3 (projections and tau), Theorem 1.4 (universal property) with the formula (1.a) of its proof 1.6, Definition 1.7; p. 171-174 of the arXiv numbering
